weather_line: Pine-scented on the eastern ridge · hat weather · the Jeep is watching

stories.headline: The Fifth Duck Arrives; Its Hat Contains a Monogram; the Investigation Enters Its Final Act
stories.byline: By our Expedition and Creature Desk correspondent
body: At approximately quarter past seven this morning, a fifth rubber duck was discovered on the Jeep's bonnet, positioned precisely on the centre seam — deliberate placement, say analysts — secured by what the Department of Magical Fibres has confirmed is the same pre-1980 Sticking Charm as its predecessor. The duck is teal. Its hat is extraordinary: a miniature flat cap, hand-stitched in copper-green fabric, with a silk lining and a small brim that moves, slightly, in wind. It is, by several measures, the finest chapeau yet produced by the Duck Bandit.

But the hat is not the news. The news is the monogram. Stitched in white thread on the cap's inner band — visible only when the hat is carefully removed, which Lucy accomplished within forty seconds of discovery, by methods she declined to describe — are two letters: E.H.

Lucy has carried this intelligence from the Jeep to the kitchen table and back to the Jeep twice since breakfast. Steve has photographed the monogram and cross-referenced it against the 1978 wood conditioner tin, which, he reports, has no maker's mark but does have two initials scratched into the base with a nail. They are not legible. He is working on them.

stories.headline: Tuesday's Ledger Completes Without Incident; Griphook the Younger Observed Holding the Door; the Door Was Held
body: Tuesday's full vault queue moved through the Gringotts third floor with what senior staff are describing, in hushed tones, as 'frictionless momentum.' Three accounts were reconciled, one long-standing dispute over compound interest was resolved in eight minutes by the simple application of the relevant clause and a look that required no further elaboration, and a delegation from the Transylvania office left satisfied, which is not something the Transylvania office has done in living memory.

Griphook the Younger, stationed at the east-corridor door at the close of business, was observed holding it open as Christine passed. No reason was given. No reason was requested. The act was accepted in the spirit in which, it is assumed, it was intended.

stories.headline: Prentice-Hoole's Unnamed Body Holds Its First Meeting; Agrees Only on the Agenda for the Second Meeting; Adjourns
body: The seven-word body established last week by Undersecretary Prentice-Hoole — formally titled the Provisional Working Group on Unregistered Upland Terrain Features and Matters Arising — convened at eleven o'clock Tuesday in Room Fourteen, a room with a low ceiling and no natural light, which observers agree suits the endeavour.

The full session lasted twenty-two minutes and produced a single agreed document: a draft agenda for the next meeting, which includes, as item three, 'Review and possible amendment of the current agenda.' Junior clerk Tibbs, reached for comment at his reinstated desk, said he had no comment and looked at the framed apology on his wall for a moment before returning to his work.

stories.headline: The Initials on the Tin's Base Yield One Letter With Certainty; Steve Has Arranged Good Lighting for the Second
body: Working in the shed under conditions he describes as 'improved since Monday,' Steve has confirmed that the first initial scratched into the base of the Eastern Ridge Blend wood conditioner tin (circa 1978) is, definitively, the letter E. The second initial, partially obscured by what appears to be sixty years of shed contact with a wooden shelf, is partially resolved. Steve has introduced a lamp. He expects a further report by evening.
The Jeep, which has been parked facing the eastern ridge since yesterday afternoon, is either monitoring developments or simply parked. Steve believes both things may be true.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Has removed and replaced the monogrammed hat three times today — the third time, she placed it back on the duck at a slightly different angle than it started. When asked why, she looked at the kitchen table, then at the door, and left the room at a pace that was not quite running.

Ellie: Discovered her reflection in the Jeep's passenger-side mirror this morning and spent several warm minutes greeting it. Has since visited twice more. Reports that her reflection is very consistent and quite friendly.

Jersey: Successfully relocated from the armchair to the kitchen table chair during breakfast, citing superior warmth near the window. The armchair has not been formally vacated. He is maintaining options.
founding_editor_note: Two letters on a tin base aren't a mystery — they're a measurement. Once you know the first one, you build from there. That's how it always works. — D.

in_brief.sport: The Interguild Strongwitch Invitational postponed; organisers cite 'insufficient ceiling height' at the proposed venue; Christine unavailable for comment as she is dealing with the Transylvania correspondence.
in_brief.forecast: Clearing by midday on the eastern ridge; good light for close work in the shed; the monogram legible, probably, if you look from the right angle.

storyline_updates.title: The Duck Bandit
storyline_updates.summary: Day 4: The fifth duck has arrived — teal, with a hand-stitched copper-green flat cap containing a white-thread monogram, 'E.H.,' on the inner band. Lucy found the monogram within forty seconds. Steve has confirmed the first initial on the conditioner tin base is E; the second is partially legible under improved lighting. The Bandit's shape is very nearly in focus: the initials E.H., pre-1980 charm-work, old-growth eastern ridge, a practitioner who learned before Ministry licensing, and a talent for millinery. Day 5 should be the reveal — Steve resolves the second initial on the tin (H), the name E.H. clicks into place, the Bandit is identified (a figure connected to the eastern ridge, older, known to at least one of them or to the family, who has been leaving ducks as a form of wordless affection or trail-marking). The reveal should be warm and satisfying, not dramatic. Lucy should be acknowledged as having known substantially longer than anyone else.
